ns2:section.sectionText: This course will introduce students to the fundamentals of the finite element method as it is used in engineering modeling, design, and optimization. The finite element method is widely used to solve problems with inhomogeneous materials and complex boundary conditions. We will discuss one- and two-dimensional elements, coordinate systems, field problems (heat transfer and fluid flow problems), structural analysis, elasticity, evaluation and verification of numerical solutions, and computer-aided design and optimization of biomedical components. Applications will span multiscale physiology and bioengineering technologies. Prerequisites: BIOE 298, BIOE 201, and MATH 285, or their equivalents
ns2:section.sectionDeptRestriction: Restricted to students in the Bioengineering department.
